open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks run at startup when check_installed_instances has no operation name or proposed ports, and in what order are failures across capabilities selected?
options: Validate only service-record and selected-instance structure needed to inspect required headers
Validate every capability's operation-independent fields in manifest order
Apply the full proposal checks to only operations referenced by existing bindings
open_points.default_guess: Validate only the service record, selected instance and required headers needed for the credential-header collision check.

open_points.subject: installation.manifest_source and manifest readers
open_points.text: “Return the manifest location and revision fixed at start” and “reads <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured revision”
open_points.question: How is manifest_revision applied when reading a record: as an immutable VCS object, as verification of an already checked-out directory, or by some other mechanism?
options: Read the file directly from the named VCS revision without changing the checkout
Read the working directory and verify that its current revision matches
Treat manifest_location as a revision-addressable storage API
open_points.default_guess: Read the file from the immutable VCS tree identified by manifest_revision.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list
open_points.text: “takes from it only the token list. Exactly four checks apply to a re-read: the file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two tokens are equal; no two agent tokens share a name”
open_points.question: During a token-list reread, what happens when the JSON parses but the owner-token or agent-token structure is absent, duplicated, wrongly typed, or otherwise invalid?
options: Treat token-list structural validation as part of ‘parsed’ and return no valid list
Reuse the last structurally valid token layout while replacing only present values
Treat absent or malformed token fields as an empty token list
open_points.default_guess: Treat any malformed or missing token-list structure as a failed reread and return no valid list.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request base URL
open_points.text: “The URL is the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path” while api_base_url need only be “an absolute http or https URL with a host”
open_points.question: Are user-info, query, fragment, and path components allowed in api_base_url, and exactly how are multiple trailing slashes and an existing base path joined to the declared path?
options: Reject user-info, query and fragment; preserve a base path and remove exactly one joining slash
Require an origin-only base URL with no path, query, fragment or user-info
Allow every absolute URL and use an HTTP library's URL-resolution rules
open_points.default_guess: Reject user-info, query and fragment, preserve an optional base path, strip trailing slashes, and append the declared absolute path deterministically.

open_points.subject: service_invoker multipart field construction
open_points.text: “Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>", with filename="<port>" added for a file part”
open_points.question: How are port names containing quotes, backslashes, control characters or other characters unsafe in a MIME quoted string encoded or refused?
options: Restrict multipart port names to a safe character set when the binding is proposed
Escape them using a specified MIME quoted-string algorithm
Fail request preparation as input_not_placeable
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a binding requiring multipart when a port name cannot be inserted safely without escaping.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox
open_points.text: “bubblewrap is present and one probe execution succeeds”
open_points.question: What code, inputs, ports, resource bounds and assertions constitute the probe, and which sandbox properties must it demonstrate before startup succeeds?
options: Run only a minimal conforming no-op implementation and confirm cleanup
Exercise namespace isolation, environment, traps, limits and cleanup in one defined probe suite
Check bubblewrap invocation separately and run a minimal Python process
open_points.default_guess: Run a fixed minimal conforming implementation through the complete normal runner and require successful cleanup and the specified environment.

open_points.subject: sandbox.execute_function malformed returns
open_points.text: “The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every value output and the bytes of every file output” and “the returned dict does not have exactly the output ports, or a value fails its port's schema … — contract_violation”
open_points.question: How is output_bytes enforced, and which outcome is returned, when run returns a non-dict, extra keys, non-JSON Python objects, cyclic values, or values that cannot be canonically encoded?
options: Bound the runner's raw result channel first, then classify any representational or schema defect as contract_violation
Count only declared conforming outputs and classify encoding failures as crashed
Validate the return first and apply output_bytes only after it conforms
open_points.default_guess: Bound the raw result channel before decoding; if within the bound, classify malformed, non-JSON or nonconforming returns as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: trial execution value outputs
open_points.text: “record_trial_execution … writes one TrialExecution M07 and the StoredValues of its value outputs” while sandbox.execute_function says “stored_value_bytes_max … [is] not the sandbox's — runs and store apply [it] after the execution”
open_points.question: What happens when a successful trial or admission execution returns a value output larger than stored_value_bytes_max but within the contract's output_bytes bound?
options: Change the trial outcome to contract_violation with value_too_large
Store the oversized value because trial outputs use output_bytes only
Keep only its digest and size without a StoredValue
open_points.default_guess: Classify the trial execution as contract_violation with value_too_large and do not store the oversized value.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.send_prepared_request failure_detail
open_points.text: “One outcome name … and a bounded failure_detail”
open_points.question: What failure_detail is returned for transport failures with no response body, such as DNS failure, TLS failure, timeout, reset or EOF, and how is it made stable and free of paths or secrets?
options: No failure_detail for failures without a response body
A fixed closed diagnostic for each transport category
A sanitized transport-library exception message
open_points.default_guess: Return no failure_detail when there is no response body; use the outcome and detail code as the diagnostic.

open_points.subject: agent masking of failure_detail
open_points.text: “a classified failure_detail [is returned] only as its length and class”
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 bytes
Unicode code points
Characters after replacement and truncation

open_points.subject: store.spool_file replacement accounting
open_points.text: “a spooled file no record names, left by a change that failed, is replaced at its position” and unnamed files remain “counted toward spool_run_bytes_max … until … a later write to the same position replaces them”
open_points.question: When replacing an unnamed file at the same spool position, is the old file's size subtracted before checking spool_run_bytes_max, and must replacement plus accounting be atomic?
options: Subtract the old position's size, check the resulting total, then atomically replace it
Count old and new bytes simultaneously until the rename completes
Remove the old file first and then perform an ordinary new-file ceiling check
open_points.default_guess: Compute the ceiling against the run total with the old position removed, then atomically replace it.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file ceiling cleanup
open_points.text: “refused over a spool ceiling, nothing kept of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before”
open_points.question: What result and residual state are required if deleting files already spooled by that attempt fails while handling a ceiling refusal?
options: Return internal_error and stop the kernel, leaving any undeleted files unnamed
Still return the ceiling refusal and defer cleanup to startup
Retry cleanup until all attempt files are gone before returning
open_points.default_guess: Return internal_error, leave any remnants unnamed, and rely on process restart and later spool removal for cleanup.
